chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog of the Magian — the Muslim man takes it, then he says Bismillah when he releases it [to hunt]. May he eat from what it catches for him? He (AS) said: 'Yes, because it is a trained hunting animal and the Name of Allah has been mentioned over it.'

key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيُّ: Magian; a Zoroastrian fire-worshipper; in classical Islamic jurisprudence, Magians (Majus) occupy a distinct legal status from Muslims, Christians, and Jews
key_terms.ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ: mentioned the Name of Allah; i.e., said 'Bismillah' at the moment of sending the hunting animal — a required condition for the lawfulness of the hunt
key_terms.مُكَلَّبٌ: trained hunting animal (especially a dog); a technical jurisprudential term indicating an animal specially trained to hunt and retain prey for the hunter

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat prey caught by a Magian's dog if a Muslim says Bismillah when releasing it?
ai.summary: Sulayman ibn Khalid asks Imam al-Sadiq whether a Muslim may eat prey caught by a Magian's (Zoroastrian's) dog, provided the Muslim says Bismillah upon releasing it. The Imam rules it permissible because the dog is trained (mukallabun) and the Name of Allah was invoked at the moment of release. This hadith establishes that the permissibility of game caught by a hunting dog depends on two conditions: the dog being trained (mukallab) and the hunter invoking Allah's name — not on the ownership or religious affiliation of the dog's original owner.
